items.description: Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net.
items.readme:
# Handwired

Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net; no training, exact, yet also fully differentiable!

## How It Works

A program's made of if-else, loops, and state. Handwired transforms them into matrix multiplication + reglu over floats. For example:

```ts
const a = 5
const result = (a > 4) ? 10 : 12
```

The above can be expressed as basic arithmetic:

```ts
const a = 5
// Math.max(0, x) is ReLU. For an integer a, above4 is 1 if a > 4, and 0 otherwise
const above4 = Math.max(0, a - 4) - Math.max(0, a - 5)
// Both branches compute, and above4 picks one
const result = above4 * 10 + (1 - above4) * 12
```

You can calculate that by hand and see that both arrive at the same result.

We then collect the + and * and relu into a giant matmul, and either run it on JS or WebGPU, for fun.

Because we basically only use these 2 primitives:
- the full program stays differentiable
- the weights don't need training since they're written manually
- existing gpu techniques, such as fusion, sparsity, reordering, have a great time optimizing such minimal primitives

This unlocks lots of funny use-cases, like:
- unfreezing the weights and train them (what does that even do? Let's find out!)
- attaching a specific frozen program to a generic neural net and train end-to-end (now a nanoGPT can do both Shakespeare and your particular UI?)
- achieving GPU-level of parallelism with JS code that was written in a traditional single-threaded way (see the JSON search demo that runs in milliseconds over 100k documents)

## Play With It

Try the demos live: https://chenglou.me/handwired/

`git clone && bun install`, then `bun start` to run them locally. Check `docs/`, `src/` and `template/` to get started! (`lab/` is a bunch of old experiments you can check or ignore)

![HandwiredOS](assets/demos-handwiredos.webp)

items.description: Open-source version of Scion: version control built for coding agents.
items.readme:
# open_scion

**Source control for the age of coding agents.**

Anthropic built **Scion**, a faster version control system for coding agents,
and described it in
[Redesigning source control](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control):
a server-centric system built for hundreds of agents that read, write and land
code at the same time. Scion is internal to Anthropic and is not available to
the public.

So I built **open_scion**: an open-source version of that design that anyone can
run, and that the community can improve and maintain together.

MIT licensed. Vendor neutral: the server never calls a language model, and every
AI feature works with any provider, or none.

<sub>open_scion is an independent implementation of the publicly described design. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.</sub>

---

## Why

Classic Git hosting was built for humans who clone a repository, work for hours
and push once. Coding agents work differently: thousands of short-lived tasks,
each touching a few files, each wanting to land in seconds, all on the same
branches. Full clones, merge queues and client-side history walks become the
bottleneck.

Scion's answer is to move the work to the server: clients stay online and fetch
only what they need, history questions are answered (and cached) by the server,
changes land through a compare-and-swap instead of a queue, every update is an
entry in a changeset log, and the repository state lives in a consistent
database plus object storage so servers scale out. open_scion implements these
ideas, with normal Git repositories underneath.

## The Scion ideas, implemented

| Scion idea | In open_scion |
|---|---|
| **Always-online clients** that fetch exactly what they need | `ObjectService` serves single objects and sparse trees; `graft clone` and `graft sparse` materialize only the paths you ask for. |
| **Source control as an API**: history runs on the server | Blame, path history, ancestry and code search run server-side and are memoized as derived data, computed once per commit. |
| **Landing without a merge queue** | `UserLand` rebases a change onto the current tip and lands it with a compare-and-swap; concurrent lands on one branch are batched into a single reference update. |
| **Automatic conflict resolution** | A conflicting land is resolved by a resolver you choose (any LLM provider, a deterministic tool, or none) through a versioned, vendor-neutral protocol. |
| **Changeset log** | Every accepted reference update is recorded with its operation and actor in a dense, ordered log that clients list or watch live. |
| **Storage core: a database and object storage, stateless servers** | Each change is a changeset in a write-ahead log in SQLite or PostgreSQL, with a compare-and-swap per reference; packs live in object storage (file, S3, GCS, Azure). Server nodes are caches that any node can rebuild, so you add nodes to scale. |
| **Test after landing, revert the culprit** | `graft-verify` tests the tip, bisects a failure and reverts the change that broke it. |
| **Monitoring agents ("superfans")** | Agents follow the changeset stream and report what matters to each component, also through Slack. |
| **Agent-friendly review** | Reviews with semantic approval rules: a comment-only change can need fewer approvals than a logic change. |
| **Agents as first-class users** | Per-agent tokens, an RPC allowlist and branch policies decide what each agent may do. |
| **Strict cache tiers** | `graft-cache` caches immutable objects in daemon and regional tiers, verifying every object. |

## Architecture

```
        agents, CI jobs, sparse workspaces          graft CLI / Go SDK
                            |
                            v   gRPC
        +-------------------------------------------------+
        |  graft-cache (optional daemon and cache tiers)  |
        +------------------------+------------------------+
                                 v
   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
   |  open_scion server (any number of nodes)                      |
   |  land - objects - changesets - derived data - search - review |
   |  write path: changeset + compare-and-swap per reference       |
   +-----------+--------------------------------+------------------+
               |                                |
               v                                v
   +-----------------------+       +-----------------------------+
   |  SQLite / PostgreSQL  |       |  object storage             |
   |  changeset WAL, refs, |       |  content-addressed packs    |
   |  changelog, reviews   |       |  (file, S3, GCS, Azure)     |
   +-----------------------+       +-----------------------------+
               \                              /
                local Git repositories = caches any node can rebuild
```

Details: [ARCHITECTURE.md](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and [STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md).

## Quick start

Requirements: Linux or macOS, Go 1.26, a C toolchain, Meson and Ninja (the
build compiles a bundled Git).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/feder-cr/open_scion.git
cd open_scion
make build                         # server, CLI and tools into _build/bin
examples/graft/quickstart.sh       # a server, a cache daemon, two agents and a land, in a temporary directory
./_build/bin/graft                 # the CLI and its commands
```

To run your own server, adapt [`examples/graft/config.toml`](examples/graft/config.toml)
and start it with `_build/bin/gitaly serve config.toml`. To put the repository
state in a database and object storage, add a `[graft.storage]` section: start in
`shadow` mode, import your repositories, then switch to `authoritative`
([STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md)).

Inside the code the extensions are called **Graft**: the `[graft]`
configuration section, the `graft` CLI, `internal/graft` and `doc/graft`.

## Documentation

- [Quickstart](doc/graft/QUICKSTART.md) and [configuration reference](doc/graft/CONFIGURATION.md)
- [Architecture](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and the [storage core](doc/graft/STORAGE.md)
- [Landing and batching](doc/graft/LAND-BATCHING.md), [conflict resolution](doc/graft/RESOLVE.md), [derived data](doc/graft/DERIVED.md)
- [Review](doc/graft/REVIEW.md), [search](doc/graft/SEARCH.md), [verification](doc/graft/VERIFY.md), [superfans](doc/graft/SUPERFAN.md) and [Slack chat](doc/graft/SUPERFAN-CHAT.md)
- [Agent security](doc/graft/AGENT-SECURITY.md), [benchmarks](doc/graft/BENCH.md), [fuzzing](doc/graft/FUZZING.md)
- [Limitations and roadmap](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md)
- Design documents of each phase: [PLAN.md](doc/graft/PLAN.md) to [PLAN6.md](doc/graft/PLAN6.md)

## Status

Version 0.1.0, the first public release. Everything above is implemented and
covered by unit, end-to-end, multi-node, crash and fuzz tests. Interfaces may
still change before 1.0. Known gaps (for example garbage collection of packs in
the storage core) are listed in [LIMITATIONS.md](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md).

## Community

open_scion is meant to be maintained by its community. Open an issue to report a
bug or propose an idea, start a discussion before a large design change, and send
pull requests: tests and a short description of the reasoning make them easy to
review. The design documents in `doc/graft/PLAN*.md` explain why things are the
way they are.

## Credits and license

open_scion is MIT licensed, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

It started as a fork of [Gitaly](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitaly), GitLab's
Git RPC server (MIT, Copyright GitLab Inc.), which provides the Git plumbing
underneath; every upstream Gitaly RPC keeps working. The non-MIT `ee/` directory
of upstream Gitaly is not part of this repository. Gitaly's own README is kept in
[doc/UPSTREAM-GITALY.md](doc/upstream/README-GITALY.md), and third-party notices are in
[NOTICE](NOTICE).

# Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection for Windows

**Uncharted 1, 2 and 3 from the PS4 collection running natively on Windows 10 and 11, by [SuperMedo](https://github.com/Supermedo).** Mohammed Albarghouthi

Same idea as my [Bloodborne port](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc): the original PS4 game
code runs directly on your PC and the graphics are translated to Vulkan. Unpack the zip, start
`Uncharted.exe`, pick your game folder, choose a game and press **PLAY**.

**[Download the latest version](https://github.com/Supermedo/uncharted_pc/releases/latest)** · **[Join the Discord]([https://discord.gg/yTMG8c4Bqm](https://discord.gg/s3RgH6cRfJ))**

> **No game files are included.** You need your own decrypted dump of the collection
> (CUSA02343, CUSA02320, ...: the folder with eboot.bin, big2-ps4_Shipping.elf,
> big3-ps4_Shipping.elf, sce_sys, u1data, u2data and u3data).
> This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog.

## Features

- All three games from one launcher: Drake's Fortune, Among Thieves and Drake's Deception.
- 60 FPS like on PS4, or 120 FPS (higher rates are experimental).
- Anti-aliasing with TAA, AMD FSR 3.1, AMD FSR 4 or NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA).
- Frame generation: AMD FSR 3 (any GPU) or NVIDIA DLSS (RTX 40 2x, RTX 50 up to 4x).
- Keyboard, mouse and controller together, all remappable. Mouse look in U3.
- Add to Steam and desktop shortcuts from the launcher, automatic updates.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 (1903 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit.
- A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and a current driver.
- About 8 GB of free memory (RAM + page file).

## Known problems

- **Uncharted 3, Cartagena square (chapter 2):** at high frame rates (240 Hz setting, ~80 FPS)
  the game could freeze and close with "GPU crash: the graphics device was lost". It came from
  the speed fix for that area and is fixed in 0.3. If it still happens to you, set Frame rate to
  60 on the Display page and open an issue with your `user\last_run.log`.
- **Uncharted 3:** green or black shapes flash for a single frame on some characters (Sully's
  shirt in Cartagena). It happens in shadPS4 too, so it's a shader translation problem. Not fixed yet.
- **Crash with "ASSERTION: GetRenderFrameParams(frameToFreeInstancesFor)->m_gfxEopTick":** the
  game got too many frames ahead of the GPU side while it was busy (building shaders on a first
  run). 0.3.1 holds the game at most one frame ahead, like on PS4. If you still see it, open an
  issue with your log.
- Frame rates above 120 are experimental.

## Building

MSYS2 CLANG64 on Windows: `bash build.sh` builds `out\bb-probe.exe`, and
`bash packaging/windows/package.sh` makes `dist\uncharted-windows` and the zip.

## Credits

Built on [bbport](https://github.com/deadinside28/bloodborne_pc), the native Linux port of
Bloodborne by deadinside28, and on the [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)
renderer. Video decoding (Videodec2) and the DLSS bridge come from
[IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR](https://github.com/IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR).
Thanks to Mindro for the shadPS4 Uncharted build that showed which problems to look for.

Also used: [FSR-Vulkan](https://github.com/FireBurn/FSR-Vulkan) and the AMD FidelityFX SDK (FSR),
FSR 4 assets from [FireBurn/Q2RTX](https://github.com/FireBurn/Q2RTX), the
[NVIDIA DLSS SDK](https://github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS) (`nvngx_dlss.dll` under NVIDIA's license),
[LibAtrac9](https://github.com/Thealexbarney/LibAtrac9), [SDL3](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL),
[FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org), [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui),
[sirit](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/sirit), [magic_enum](https://github.com/Neargye/magic_enum),
[xbyak](https://github.com/herumi/xbyak),
[Vulkan Memory Allocator](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator),
[MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org) / [LLVM](https://llvm.org), [PyInstaller](https://pyinstaller.org),
[Pillow](https://python-pillow.org) and the Cinzel font (SIL Open Font License).

NVIDIA, GeForce RTX and DLSS are trademarks of NVIDIA Corporation. The default covers and the
icon are original artwork; no official art is included.

## License

GNU GPL v2 or later ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). Third-party components keep their own licenses
(see `licenses\` in the download).

# Legislação brasileira em Markdown

**323.849 normas** — a Constituição Federal, a legislação federal e a de 25 estados e do Distrito
Federal — convertidas de fontes oficiais para Markdown, com cabeçalho estruturado e link para a
origem de cada texto.

O histórico do git é a própria linha do tempo: as 323.849 normas da base entraram **uma por
commit**, assinadas por quem as promulgou e datadas do dia em que foram aprovadas.

O objetivo é maior do que o que já está aqui: **todo o ordenamento jurídico brasileiro** — leis,
decretos, atos infralegais das agências e órgãos reguladores, tratados internalizados,
jurisprudência vinculante e o direito estadual e municipal — num lugar só, em texto simples, de
graça, para qualquer pessoa.

[![progresso](progresso.svg)](PROGRESSO.md)

O escopo completo está em [`scripts/plano.py`](scripts/plano.py) e a medição item a item — o que
já tem, o que falta, de que fonte vem e em qual pasta fica — em **[PROGRESSO.md](PROGRESSO.md)**,
gerados por `scripts/progresso.py`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Os textos têm caráter informativo e **não substituem a publicação no Diário Oficial**. São
> conversões automáticas e, em 17.016 arquivos, OCR de PDF escaneado. Confira sempre a fonte
> indicada no cabeçalho antes de citar.

---

## O que tem aqui

| Esfera | Normas |
| --- | ---: |
| Constituição Federal | 1 |
| Federal | 29.184 |
| Estadual e distrital | 294.664 |
| **Total** | **323.849** |

Por tipo de instrumento:

| Tipo | Normas | | Tipo | Normas |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| Lei Ordinária | 289.684 | | Lei Promulgada | 434 |
| Decreto-Lei | 18.366 | | Emenda à Lei Orgânica | 134 |
| Lei Complementar | 12.598 | | Constituição Estadual | 26 |
| Emenda Constitucional | 2.013 | | Decreto-Lei Complementar | 23 |
| Lei Delegada | 550 | | Lei Constitucional | 19 |

As contagens por estado, com o que ficou de fora e por quê, estão em
**[COBERTURA.md](COBERTURA.md)**. Para ver em gráficos — normas por estado, por década, por tema,
as palavras mais frequentes nas ementas e quem mais assinou — abra
**[estatisticas.html](estatisticas.html)** no navegador. É um arquivo único, sem servidor nem
dependência externa, gerado por `scripts/estatisticas.py`.

---

## Estrutura

```
constituicao.md                      Constituição Federal de 1988 (texto vigente, Planalto)
federal/
  leis-ordinarias/AAAA/*.md          Leis federais, de 1822 a hoje
  leis-complementares/AAAA/*.md
  leis-delegadas/  decretos-lei/
estaduais/UF/
  constituicao/                      Constituição estadual
  emendas-constitucionais/
  leis-ordinarias/  leis-complementares/  leis-delegadas/  decretos-lei/
reguladores/<orgao>/<tipo>/          atos infralegais federais (CONTRAN, ANVISA, RFB, CMN…)
jurisprudencia/<tribunal>/           súmulas, temas vinculantes e controle concentrado
tratados/                            tratados internacionais internalizados
municipais/UF/<municipio>/           legislação municipal
scripts/                             o código que baixa, converte e audita
scripts/plano.py                     o escopo: todo tipo de norma que deve estar aqui
COBERTURA.md                         números por esfera e tipo, e as lacunas
PROGRESSO.md                         o plano medido contra o acervo, item a item
progresso.svg                        a imagem de progresso do topo deste README
estatisticas.html                    página com gráficos sobre o acervo
```

Os nomes de pasta são os mesmos em todas as esferas. Algumas unidades têm pastas a mais, porque a
fonte distingue instrumentos que as outras não têm: `leis-promulgadas` (AM, PB),
`decretos-lei-complementares` (SP), `leis-constitucionais` (MG), `constituicoes-historicas` (BA),
`lei-organica` e `emendas-lei-organica` (DF).

Fora do versionamento, porque os scripts os reproduzem: `_fonte/` (27 GB com o HTML e os PDFs
originais, comprimidos), `_indice/` (os índices de cada fonte) e os logs. Os `_falhas.jsonl`, que
registram linha por linha o que não entrou, **estão** versionados.

---

## Formato dos arquivos

Todo arquivo tem cabeçalho YAML e, no corpo, o título em `#` seguido do texto da norma:

```markdown
---
titulo: "Lei nº 10.406 de 10/01/2002"
uf: "SP"                 # ausente nas normas federais
tipo: "Lei Ordinária"
numero: "10406"
data: 2002-01-10         # sempre presente; vazia quando a fonte não informa
ano: "2002"              # só quando a fonte dá apenas o ano (PA, PE)
ementa: "Institui o Código Civil."
situacao: "Em vigor"
revogada: false
versao_texto: "compilada (texto vigente)"
publicacao: "DOU de 11/01/2002"
data_publicacao: 2002-01-11
urn: "urn:lex:br:federal:lei:2002-01-10;10406"
fonte: "https://normas.leg.br/?urn=urn:lex:br:federal:lei:2002-01-10;10406"
arquivo: "https://…/lei10406.pdf"   # quando o texto veio de um PDF
baixado_em: 2026-10-13
---
# Lei nº 10.406 de 10/01/2002

LEI Nº 10.406, DE 10 DE JANEIRO DE 2002

Institui o Código Civil.
```

`titulo`, `tipo`, `numero`, `data`, `versao_texto`, `fonte` e `baixado_em` existem em **todos** os
arquivos; os demais aparecem quando a fonte os fornece. Os campos saem sempre nessa ordem.

O campo `tipo` usa um vocabulário fechado de onze valores, definido em `CANONICO`, em
`scripts/comum.py`. O mesmo mapa vale para quem baixa e para `scripts/normalizar.py`, que o reaplica
ao acervo já gravado — por isso `lei-ordinaria` e `leis-ordinarias`, ou `Lei` e `LEI ORDINARIA`, não
coexistem.

Duas exceções, ambas propositais: a `constituicao.md` na raiz é o único arquivo sem cabeçalho, por
ser o documento único de topo; e cinco arquivos trazem, no lugar do texto, um aviso em citação —
a fonte oficial serve um documento vazio para eles e só os metadados foram preservados.

---

## O histórico do git

A base do histórico é uma linha do tempo da legislação: **323.851 commits**, um por norma, em
ordem cronológica de 1822 até hoje, cada um assinado por quem promulgou a norma — **5.414
autores**. Foi montada de uma vez só por `scripts/montar_repositorio.py`, com `git fast-import`.

> [!NOTE]
> **As normas que chegam depois entram em commits de lote**, um por coleta — "153.637 decretos
> federais (1889–2026)" —, não mais um commit por norma. Reconstruir a linha do tempo a cada lote
> significaria reescrever e reenviar meio milhão de commits para acrescentar texto novo; o custo
> não se paga. A linha do tempo norma a norma continua no histórico e continua verdadeira para o
> que ela cobre, e `montar_repositorio.py` continua funcionando para quem quiser gerá-la de novo,
> do acervo inteiro, num repositório à parte.

Os autores que mais assinaram, na base:

| Normas | Signatário |
| ---: | --- |
| 4.247 | Marconi Ferreira Perillo Júnior |
| 3.795 | Aécio Neves |
| 3.457 | Geraldo Alckmin |
| 3.097 | Ronaldo Caiado |
| 2.654 | Getúlio Vargas |

O autor sai do bloco de assinatura do próprio texto (`scripts/signatarios.py`). Em cerca de 48% dos
casos a assinatura não está na camada de texto do PDF, ou o OCR a perdeu; nesses, o autor é a
instituição — "Estado do Pará", "República Federativa do Brasil". **A mensagem do commit sempre diz
de onde a autoria saiu**, na linha `Autoria:`. Os demais signatários entram como `Co-Authored-By`.

Os e-mails são sintéticos, no formato `nome-sobrenome-NNNNN@exemplo.com`, com os cinco dígitos
derivados do próprio nome — cada pessoa tem uma identidade só no histórico inteiro.

> [!NOTE]
> **Datas anteriores a 1970.** O git conta a data em segundos desde 1970; qualquer data anterior
> vira timestamp negativo, que o `git fsck` reprova como `badDate` e o GitHub rejeita ao receber.
> Como a maior parte do acervo é anterior a 1970, essas normas têm a data do commit fixada em
> 01-01-1970 e a **data real no fim do título, depois de ` | `**, e repetida no corpo. Nos commits
> com data representável o título fica limpo. A ordem cronológica se mantém pela sequência de
> commits, que é linear.

```
Lei nº 86, de 21/04/1880 | 21-04-1880

AUTORIZA O GOVERNO A DISPENSAR DE PROVAS DE CAPACIDADE PARA EXERCER O MAGISTÉRIO…

Data da norma: 1880-04-21
A data do commit está fixada em 01-01-1970: o git não representa data anterior a essa
(vira timestamp negativo, que o GitHub rejeita). A data real da norma é a do título e
a da linha acima.
Autoria: signatário não identificado no texto; autoria institucional.
Fonte: https://www.al.sp.gov.br/norma/139216
```

As 1.595 normas cuja data não existe em nenhuma fonte ficam no fim do histórico, com
`| sem data na fonte` no título.

---

## Fontes

| UF | Fonte | Texto |
| --- | --- | --- |
| — | Planalto | Constituição Federal, texto vigente |
| Federal | Dados abertos do Senado (índice) + normas.leg.br (texto) | compilado vigente quando existe; senão a publicação original |
| AC, AL, AM, PB, PI, RO, RR, TO | SAPL das Assembleias (API REST) | PDF anexado, com OCR quando escaneado |
| AP | e-Legis da Assembleia | texto integral em PDF + Constituição consolidada |
| BA | Portal de Legislação (Casa Civil) | HTML |
| CE | BELT – Banco Eletrônico de Leis Temáticas | HTML |
| DF | SINJ-DF | texto compilado |
| ES, SE | sistema de legislação das Assembleias | HTML, compilado quando disponível |
| GO | Legisla Goiás (Casa Civil) | HTML |
| MA | GED da Assembleia | PDF |
| MG | Dados abertos da ALMG | texto atualizado quando existe |
| MS | Legislação da Governadoria (Lotus Notes) | HTML |
| MT | Assembleia Legislativa | redação atual, PDF gerado pelo site |
| PA | Banco de Leis da ALEPA | PDF, com OCR quando escaneado |
| PE | Alepe Legis | texto atualizado quando existe |
| PR | Sistema Estadual de Legislação | — ver pendências |
| RJ | Legislação Estadual da ALERJ (Lotus Notes) | — ver pendências |
| RN | Assembleia Legislativa | PDF, acervo a partir de 1994 |
| RS | Sistema LEGIS da Assembleia; Constituição no portal do DAL | PDF nas recentes, HTML nas antigas |
| SC | Legislação SC (ALESC) | texto anotado |
| SP | ALESP (dados abertos + API) | texto atualizado quando existe |

Cada script em `scripts/estados/` documenta no cabeçalho a API ou o caminho que usa.

Todos limitam a taxa a 1–4 requisições por segundo, são retomáveis (pulam o que já existe) e
guardam o original em `_fonte/`. **Bloqueios de acesso automatizado não são contornados.**

---

## O que ainda não está aqui

O plano inteiro, com meta e fonte por tipo de norma, está em **[PROGRESSO.md](PROGRESSO.md)**. Em
resumo, o que falta se organiza em três fases:

| Fase | O quê | Por que nessa ordem |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | Fechar a esfera federal: emendas constitucionais, decretos do Executivo (as duas séries), decretos legislativos, medidas provisórias, resoluções das Casas, regulamentos consolidados (RIR, RIPI, Aduaneiro, RPS) e tratados promulgados | fonte única e já conhecida — `normas.leg.br` e Planalto, a mesma infraestrutura do baixador federal |
| **2** | O infralegal, onde mora a norma que de fato se aplica: CONTRAN e o Manual de Sinalização, NRs do trabalho, RDC da ANVISA, IN da Receita, resoluções do CMN e do Banco Central, CONAMA, CNE, CNJ, TSE, conselhos profissionais; a jurisprudência vinculante (súmulas, repercussão geral, repetitivos, controle concentrado); e o infralegal estadual, com destaque para os 27 RICMS | uma fonte por órgão, cada uma com seu formato — é trabalho de muitos raspadores pequenos |
| **3** | Direito municipal: leis orgânicas, planos diretores, códigos tributários, de obras e de posturas, e as leis das câmaras — começando pelas 27 capitais | 5.570 fontes sem índice central; sozinho é maior que todo o resto somado |

Além disso, ficam de fora as normas cujo texto não existe na fonte ou não pôde ser obtido — cada
caso tem uma linha, com o motivo, no `_falhas.jsonl` da respectiva pasta.

### Pendências

| O quê | Por quê |
| --- | --- |
| **PR** — nada coletado | o WAF de `legislacao.pr.gov.br` devolve 403 a partir da segunda requisição. Não contornado; precisa de outra fonte ou de autorização da Casa Civil |
| **RJ** — nada coletado | o Lotus Notes da ALERJ fecha a conexão ou leva mais de 60 s por página. `scripts/estados/rj.py` está pronto para quando o servidor voltar |
| **AC** — só até 2009 | limite do SAPL da Assembleia |
| **TO** — a partir de 2020 | limite do SAPL da Assembleia |
| **RN** — a partir de 1994 | o acervo da Assembleia não tem PDF anterior |
| **RS** — 5.569 leis antigas | estão no índice, mas a página de texto responde "NORMA SEM TEXTO": nunca foram digitalizadas |
| **ES e SE** — 311 e 411 normas | o servidor da Assembleia derruba a conexão nessas mesmas normas, de forma consistente |

### Qualidade do OCR

17.016 arquivos vêm de PDF escaneado, com OCR pelo framework Vision do macOS. O texto é legível,
mas tem dois defeitos conhecidos:

- **ordem de leitura trocada** em digitalizações de duas colunas — não tem correção automática;
  precisaria de um modelo com noção de layout;
- **ordinais confundidos** (`Art. 19` por `Art. 1º`) — corrigido em 1.509 arquivos por
  `scripts/corrigir_ocr.py`, que só reescreve a corrida `19, 29, 39…` quando ela começa em 19, tem
  ao menos dois termos e a numeração resultante fica coerente. Assim um `Art. 19` legítimo, ou um
  `Art. 99` que cita outra lei, não é tocado.

`baidu/Unlimited-OCR` foi testado em Apple Silicon e não serve localmente: na resolução de treino o
encoder de visão pede ~21 GB, e numa resolução que caiba o prefill leva 221 s por página com saída
vazia. Reprocessar o lote exige GPU NVIDIA.

---

## Reproduzir e atualizar

**Requisitos:** macOS, Python 3 (só biblioteca padrão), `pdftotext` (poppler) e, para o OCR, o
framework Vision via `swiftc -O scripts/ocr.swift -o scripts/bin/ocr`.

```sh
# baixar — todos os scripts são retomáveis: pulam o que já existe
python3 -I scripts/baixar_federal.py
python3 -I scripts/estados/sp.py                # um estado por script
python3 -I scripts/estados/sapl.py baixar PB    # estados com SAPL
python3 -I scripts/estados/spl_agape.py ES      # ES e SE

# manter em ordem
python3 -I scripts/reconverter.py [UF ...]      # regenera os .md a partir de _fonte
python3 -I scripts/normalizar.py                # pastas, tipos e cabeçalhos canônicos
python3 -I scripts/corrigir_ocr.py              # ordinais do OCR
python3 -I scripts/corrigir_datas_invalidas.py  # datas que não existem no calendário
python3 -I scripts/relatorio.py                 # atualiza COBERTURA.md
python3 -I scripts/progresso.py                 # atualiza PROGRESSO.md e progresso.svg
python3 -I scripts/estatisticas.py              # atualiza estatisticas.html

# remontar o histórico do git
python3 -I scripts/montar_repositorio.py --saida /caminho/do/repo
```

Os quatro scripts de manutenção são **idempotentes** e rodam em simulação por padrão: só gravam com
`--aplicar`. Rodar de novo, depois de aplicado, relata zero mudanças.

### Auditorias que o acervo passa

| Verificação | Resultado |
| --- | --- |
| `git fsck --strict` | zero erros |
| data em todos os arquivos | 323.848 de 323.848 (a Constituição não tem cabeçalho) |
| data que existe no calendário e não está no futuro | 100% |
| nomes de pasta canônicos | 100% |
| `tipo` no vocabulário fechado | 100% |
| cabeçalho + `# título` + texto | 323.843; 5 com aviso de ausência; 1 por desenho |

---

## Licença

Os textos das normas são **atos oficiais do poder público** e, pelo art. 8º, I, da Lei nº 9.610/98,
não são objeto de proteção autoral. Os scripts deste repositório estão sob a licença MIT — veja
[LICENSE](LICENSE).

items.readme:
# c64-hw-sim

c64-hw-sim simulates the motherboard of the Commodore 64, ASSY 250407, pin
by pin. You can lift the leg of a chip, short it to ground or to +5V, pull a
chip out of its socket, or open a resistor. Then you watch what the machine
does: the picture on the monitor, the keyboard, every signal on the board.

The program knows the board's netlist (the electrical connections on the
PCB) and how each chip behaves at its pins. It knows nothing about what a
broken Commodore 64 looks like: when you simulate a broken part and the
screen fills with garbage, that garbage was computed from the circuit, not
chosen by someone who knew what to expect.

Here is an example. Lift pin 17 (A7) of the color RAM before power on, and
the machine boots and looks healthy. The CPU writes and the VIC reads with
the same wrong address, so the RAM simply aliases. Put the leg back, and
the half of the color RAM that was never written shows up as random
colors. Lift it again, and the screen is clean. A real 2114 does the same.

With this program you can do mainly two things:

1. Learn how the Commodore 64 works at a more intimate level, in a way that
   is hard to reproduce on real hardware without the risk of damaging it
   (and on most boards many chips are soldered, not socketed).
2. If you have a broken C64 and some hypothesis about what could be broken,
   simulate it with this program and perhaps gain clues, so that you can
   desolder chips in the most logical order, and desolder as few of them as
   possible (desoldering is a boring process, and every time it risks
   damaging the board...). A matching symptom is a clue, not a proof:
   different faults can look the same, and the simulation has its limits
   (see below).

Please note that **even on fast computers** this program struggles to
simulate the C64 hardware at real speed. A real C64 is simulated at 31% of
its speed on an Apple M3 Max, 39% on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 (Gorgon
Halo), and 48% on an Apple M5 Max. This is not a problem for the goals of
this program, but be warned: it is not an emulator to play games with.

![The character ROM pulled out while a BASIC program runs, then put back](docs/char-rom.gif)

Above: the classic `10 PRINT CHR$(205.5+RND(1));:GOTO 10` maze is running
when the character ROM (U5) is pulled out of its socket, and later put
back. The CPU, the RAM and the program keep working; only the shapes of
the characters are lost, as repairers know well. The scope is on the data
line D0 of the ROM socket: with the socket empty, the bus floats (the
dotted segments) whenever the VIC fetches a character shape. Shown at C64
speed.

## Acknowledgements

I (antirez) got the idea for this program while using and observing Andre
Weissflog's (floooh) chips, emulators of the 6502, VIC-II, CIA, SID and
friends that use pins as their interface. The next step was to take this
approach, with his code as a starting point, to its logical extreme:
pin-level models of every other part of the C64, the RAMs, the ROMs, the
logic chips, the PLA, and so forth.

The chip cores are floooh's chips, taken from c64-llm (zlib license). The
board comes from bwack's C64-250407-Replica-KiCad (CERN OHL). The PLA
equations come from the 82S100 read-out by Mark Smith and Marko Mäkelä.

## Building

    make
    ./c64-hw-sim [program.prg]

It runs on macOS and Linux (X11), with OpenGL. The graphics library (sokol)
and the interface library (nuklear) are in `third_party/`.

## Using it

The window shows the board, the monitor, a control panel and an
oscilloscope.

Chips are boxes named by role:

- RAM1 to RAM8 are the 4164 DRAMs. Each one holds a single bit of every
  byte: RAMn has data bit n-1.
- VRAM is the 2114 color RAM.
- BASIC, KERNAL and CHAR are the ROMs.
- PLA is the address decoder.

Zoom in to see references and address ranges. Pins show their state as a
logic probe would: red high, blue low, yellow pulsing, gray floating,
magenta when two outputs fight.

Click a pin to put it on the oscilloscope and to break it: floating,
shorted to GND, or shorted to +5V. Click a chip to pull it out. Click a
resistor, a ferrite bead or the crystal to open it. The control panel
lists the faults, each with a repair button.

The control panel also loads .prg files. They are written straight into
the DRAM chips, as a freezer cartridge would do it, so loading works on a
broken board too.

Type on your keyboard as usual. ESC is RUN/STOP, PgUp is RESTORE, TAB is
CTRL, and left ALT is C=.

## Command line

    ./c64-hw-sim --headless 200 --text --shot out.png --fault U17:removed

This runs four seconds (200 frames) without a window. It prints the text
read from the monitor picture, as a person would read it, and saves the
picture. A fault is written `REF:what` or `REF.PIN:what`:

    U17:removed   U21.14:gnd   U12.14:vcc   U9.2:open   R51:open   RP4:short

Other options:

- `--at 150:U6.17:open --at 300:repair` breaks and repairs parts while the
  C64 runs.
- `--nets` reports the nets where outputs fought.
- `C64HW_TYPE=$'PRINT 1+1\n'` types text after boot.
- `C64HW_CHECK=1` checks every KERNAL read and every VIC fetch against the
  ideal memory map.
- `--record 900:DIR --frames 90` (graphical mode) saves the window 90
  times, every 4 emulated frames from frame 900 on. This is how the GIF
  above was made.

`tests/faults.sh` runs 31 common faults. The expected symptom of each one
was written down before the simulator was run.

## How it works

`tools/kicad2c.py` turns bwack's KiCad replica of the 250407 into C tables:
216 parts, their pads, and 249 nets.

Every pin drives its net strongly, weakly (a pull-up), from a supply short,
or not at all. The strongest drive wins. Two equal drives fighting are a
contention, and low wins.

A net that nobody drives keeps its charge, and then drifts:

- to about 1.4V within microseconds, if TTL inputs load it;
- toward 0V in a fraction of a second, if only MOS inputs are on it.

MOS inputs compare that voltage, plus some noise, with their own threshold,
so a floating line can read erratically.

Power faults depend on the chip:

- A chip without VCC is dead.
- A chip without GND lets its outputs float high.
- A CMOS chip keeps running on phantom power, which reaches it through the
  protection diodes of its pins.

The noise is seeded, so a run can be repeated exactly.

`src/parts.c` models these parts at their pins:

- the glue logic;
- the ROMs;
- the DRAMs, which latch the row on /RAS and the column on /CAS;
- the color RAM;
- the PLA, with its real logic equations.

The 6510, VIC-II, CIAs and SID are cycle-accurate cores from floooh's
chips. In `src/board.c` each core sits in a socket that sees only its pins.
Each half cycle runs in three steps: the row address, then /RAS falls,
then /CAS falls. The whole board settles after each step.

PLAN.md explains the reasoning behind these choices.

## Limits

It is slow, between a third and half of real time on the computers listed
above, because every pin of every chip is simulated.

The floating and power models have the right shape, but their numbers
(thresholds, drift times, crosstalk) are guesses. They are constants in
`src/sim.c`.

These analog parts are not simulated: the video output, the SID filter,
the power supply, and the dot clock PLL.

Faults inside a chip, such as bad DRAM cells or slow parts, and bridges
between two nets are planned but not done.

items.description: macOS 菜单栏 / Windows 托盘的显示器管理工具：不依赖 DDC/CI，通过澎湃 OS 局域网接口切换输入源、调节音量
items.readme:
MonitorBar

macOS 菜单栏 / Windows 托盘里的显示器管理工具，一份 Go 代码，两端原生界面。
A menu bar (macOS) and tray (Windows) app to manage your monitor — English

## 为什么做这个 REDMI 显示器不支持 DDC/CI。 Mac 上常见的显示器工具（MonitorControl、BetterDisplay、Lunar 等）都靠 DDC/CI 控制显示器，所以在 REDMI 显示器上切换不了输入源，也调不了音量。 不过 REDMI 显示器内置澎湃 OS，开机时会在局域网提供一个遥控接口。MonitorBar 通过这个接口切换输入源（包括 DP 和 USB-C）、调节音量，不依赖 DDC/CI。软件调光、色温、分辨率、屏幕时间这些通用功能也一起做了进去，并且有 Mac 和 Windows 两个版本：两台电脑接在同一台显示器上时，在任意一台上都能一键切到另一台。 MonitorBar 只在 REDMI 显示器 G Pro 27U 2026 上测试过，不保证在你的显示器上能正常工作：不同型号的接口、信号源编号可能不一样。如果不能用，可以借助 AI 编程工具来适配：先运行 `MonitorBar --probe` 看看它识别到了什么，再让 AI 参照下面的[适配其他显示器](#适配其他显示器)一节修改代码。 ## 功能 | 分页 | 功能 | | --- | --- | | 概览 | 当前分辨率与刷新率、**切换输入源**、软件亮度、**显示器音量**、场景（日间 / 阅读 / 观影 / 夜间） | | 画面 | 场景、**跟随 MacBook 内屏亮度**、**按时间自动切换白天 / 夜晚场景**、软件调光、色温（减少蓝光）、一键恢复 | | 分辨率 | 刷新率切换，HiDPI（仅 macOS）与标准分辨率列表 | | 屏幕时间 | 今日亮屏与使用时长，最近 7 天柱状图 | - **切换输入源、调音量不需要 DDC/CI**：澎湃 OS 显示器（如 REDMI 显示器 G Pro 27U 2026）在局域网提供遥控接口，MonitorBar 自动发现并使用它。Mac 和 Windows 接在同一台显示器的不同接口上时，两边都能一键切到对方。 - **支持 DDC/CI 的显示器**：自动用 DDC/CI 调硬件背光，切换输入源、调音量，并显示对比度、锐度、RGB 增益等显示器回应的设置。 - **软件调光与色温**通过显卡的 Gamma 表实现，任何连接线、任何显示器都能用。 - **跟随内屏亮度**（MacBook + 支持 DDC/CI 的外接显示器）：内屏开启 macOS 自动亮度时，外接显示器的背光随之平滑调节，可设定外接亮度范围；手动调整会保留到内屏亮度下次变化。 - **自动切换**：在「画面」里打开后，到了设定的白天、夜晚开始时间就自动切换到对应场景（默认 07:00「日间」、19:00「夜间」，场景可选）。只在时段交替时切换，中途的手动调整会保留到下一次交替。 - **自动更新**：定期检查 GitHub 上的新版本，在面板底部提示，一键下载并重启；更新包经签名校验，只下载变化的部分。 - 显示器不支持的功能不会出现在界面上。 - 单个可执行文件，无 webview，空闲时不占 CPU；中文界面，深色主题。 ## 安装 从 [Releases](https://github.com/binaryify/MonitorBar/releases) 或 [CI 产物](https://github.com/binaryify/MonitorBar/actions) 下载： - **macOS**（Apple Silicon / Intel，macOS 12+）：打开 `.dmg`，把 MonitorBar 拖进「应用程序」。应用未签名，首次打开需右键 → 打开。第一次连接显示器时允许「查找本地网络上的设备」。 - **Windows 10 / 11**：把 `MonitorBar.exe` 和同目录的 `icon.png` 放到任意文件夹（推荐 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\MonitorBar`）后运行。托盘图标默认在 `^` 溢出区，可拖到任务栏常驻。 开机自启：默认关闭，由用户自己选择开启——面板右上角「⋯」→「登录时启动」，或命令行 `MonitorBar --open-at-login on`（`off` 关闭）。 ## 命令行 ```bash MonitorBar --show # 启动并打开面板（程序已运行时，再次启动也会打开面板） MonitorBar --probe # 打印显示器、接口、分辨率、DDC/CI 读数和局域网发现结果 MonitorBar --open-at-login on # 开机自启（off 关闭） MonitorBar --update # 检查并安装新版本 ``` ## 工作原理 MonitorBar 有三条控制显示器的通道，启动时在后台探测，哪条可用就用哪条： | 通道 | 能做什么 | 条件 | | --- | --- | --- | | 局域网遥控 | 切换输入源、调音量 | 澎湃 OS 显示器，与电脑在同一网络 | | DDC/CI | 硬件背光、输入源、音量、对比度等 | 显示器支持 DDC/CI（部分需在显示器菜单开启） | | 显卡 Gamma 表 | 软件调光、色温 | 任何显示器 | 输入源和音量优先走局域网，其次 DDC/CI；亮度有 DDC/CI 时调硬件背光，否则用软件调光。 - **局域网遥控**：澎湃 OS 的 6095 端口提供 `getsources`（信号源列表）、`changesource2`（按编号切换，能切到 DP / USB-C）、`getvolume`、`keyevent`（遥控按键，音量 ±1）。首次启动扫描所在 /24 网段找到显示器，之后记住地址。 - **DDC/CI**：macOS 通过 IOAVService 读写显示器的 I2C 总线（Apple Silicon）；Windows 通过系统的 Monitor Configuration API（dxva2）。输入源列表取自显示器的 MCCS 能力字符串。 - **macOS**：通过 [purego](https://github.com/ebitengine/purego) 调用 CoreGraphics、IOKit、AppKit（无 cgo）。 - **Windows**：通过 `syscall` 调用 user32、gdi32、dxva2、powrprof。 ## 平台差异 - **软件调光**：Windows 只接受离标准曲线不远的 Gamma（最暗约 50%），更暗时退到允许的最暗并保留色温比例，面板会提示。macOS 无此限制。退出时两端都会恢复原始曲线。 - **跟随内屏亮度**：仅 macOS（读取 DisplayServices 的内屏亮度），且需外接显示器支持 DDC/CI 背光；Windows 暂不支持。 - **亮屏统计**：macOS 读显示器休眠状态；Windows 以「空闲时长 ≥ 电源计划的关闭显示器时间」推断。 - **面板位置**：从溢出区打开时面板贴在图标上方；拿不到图标位置时（如再次启动程序打开）贴在屏幕右下角。 - 数据保存在 `~/Library/Application Support/MonitorBar`（macOS）或 `%APPDATA%\MonitorBar`（Windows）。


Windows 11 上的面板

## 开发 基于 [mygo](https://mygo.egoist.dev/)，需要 Go 1.27+（`go` 会自动下载对应工具链）。 ```bash go tool mygo dev # 开发，改动后自动重启 go test ./... # 无窗口的界面测试与单元测试 MONITORBAR_SNAPSHOTS=docs/screenshots go test -run TestSnapshots . # 重新生成截图 go tool mygo build -platform darwin/universal,windows/amd64 # 打包两端（可在 Mac 上交叉编译 Windows 版） ``` 发布：先在 `CHANGELOG.md` 写好这个版本的说明（应用内的更新提示会显示它），再推送版本标签。CI 会用仓库 Secret `MYGO_UPDATER_PRIVATE_KEY` 签名，打包 macOS dmg、Windows zip 与更新包，并创建 GitHub Release。 ```bash git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0 ``` | 路径 | 职责 | | --- | --- | | `main.go` / `app.go` | 入口、托盘图标、弹出面板的尺寸与位置 | | `store.go` | 状态与动作：只在主线程读写，网络请求在 goroutine 中，结果经 `post` 回到主线程 | | `panel.go` / `tabs.go` / `widgets.go` / `icons.go` | 界面 | | `internal/mitv` | 澎湃 OS 局域网接口与发现 | | `internal/display` | 平台层：显示器信息、分辨率、Gamma、DDC/CI、亮屏与空闲时间 | | `internal/usage` | 屏幕时间，每 30 秒采样，保留 60 天 | | `internal/schedule` | 自动切换：按设定时间判断白天或夜晚 | ## 适配其他显示器 先运行 `MonitorBar --probe`，它会打印显示器名称、原生分辨率、DDC/CI 的读数与能力字符串，以及局域网发现结果。再按情况修改： - **支持 DDC/CI，但某些设置不对**：VCP 编码在 `internal/display/ddc.go`，输入源名称在 `InputName`（个别型号与 MCCS 不一致的，加到 `inputOverrides`），面板显示哪些设置在 `store.go` 的 `controlCatalog`。 - **DDC/CI 没有响应**：先在显示器菜单里找 DDC/CI 开关。macOS 的读写协议在 `internal/display/ddc_darwin.go`，Windows 在 `ddc_windows.go`。注意部分 Mac 的 HDMI 口不传 DDC/CI，可改用 DP 或 USB-C 连接。 - **其他品牌的局域网接口**：参照 `internal/mitv` 写一个新的通道，在 `store.go` 里接入输入源和音量的路由（`sources`、`selectInput`、`setVolume`）。 ## 致谢 - [mygo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo)：Go 桌面应用框架 - [LGwebOS-menubar](https://github.com/gabrielgreco1/LGwebOS-menubar)：界面设计的灵感来源 - 图标风格参考 [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) ## English REDMI monitors do not support DDC/CI, so the usual tools (MonitorControl, BetterDisplay, Lunar) cannot switch their inputs. They run HyperOS, though, whose LAN remote API can, DP and USB-C included. MonitorBar manages an external monitor from the macOS menu bar or the Windows notification area. It switches inputs and changes volume over the LAN remote API of Xiaomi HyperOS monitors, or over DDC/CI on monitors that support it (backlight and picture controls too), dims and warms the picture through the gamma table, switches resolutions and refresh rates, and tracks screen time. # pxl **Pixel art as code.** Write a compact `.px.js` file; get PNGs, sprite sheets with JSON, animated GIFs, and a live browser viewer that replays the painting step by step as you save. Built for AI agents (it ships as a ready-made [agent skill](#use-it-with-an-ai-agent)) and pleasant for people too. No runtime dependencies, no build step: just Node ≥ 22.18.

Every image above is generated from a file in [`examples/`](examples). ## Quick start ```sh git clone https://github.com/crsolver/claude-pxl.git cd claude-pxl node bin/pxl.js serve examples/shop.px.js # live viewer at http://127.0.0.1:4321/ ``` Or run it without cloning: ```sh npx github:crsolver/claude-pxl build art.px.js ``` Write `art.px.js`: ```js pal({ k: "#1b1630", g: "#8ccf63", G: "#4c8a44", w: "#fff6e0", r: "#e2585e", R: "#a63a4c" }) // Write the left half; mirror it and outline it automatically. sprite("slime", { mx: true, outline: "k" }, ` ....ggg ..ggGGg .ggGwGg gggkwgg GGGGGGG`) sprite("slime_red", { base: "slime", swap: { g: "r", G: "R" } }) // a recolor in one line sheet("chars", ["slime*"], { pad: 1 }) ``` ```sh node bin/pxl.js build art.px.js ``` ``` out/sprites/slime.png out/sprites/slime_red.png the art, at 1x out/chars.png out/chars.json sprite sheet + TexturePacker-style JSON out/_preview/*.png upscaled previews with a pixel grid ``` ## The live viewer `pxl serve art.px.js` opens a viewer that rebuilds on every save and replays the asset you edited op by op, so you (or whoever is watching an agent work) can see the art being painted. It also writes the same `out/` files as `build`. ## Commands ``` pxl build [--out DIR] [--only a,b] [--scale N] [--no-preview] pxl serve [--port 4321] [--out DIR | --no-out] [--no-preview] pxl ascii print an asset as palette keys with x/y rulers pxl list list assets, groups and sheets with source locations ``` `pxl` means `node bin/pxl.js` in a clone, or `npx github:crsolver/claude-pxl`. Art files can be `.js` or `.ts` (`types/pxl.d.ts` gives editor completion). ## What's in the DSL - **Palettes and ramps**: one-character color keys, built-in palettes (pico8, sweetie16, endesga32…), dark→light ramps that drive `shade()` / `light()`. - **Sprites**: text grids, mirroring, auto-outline, palette-swap variants, flips/rotations, reusable `_parts`, `stamp`. - **Primitives and brushes**: rects, lines, circles, polygons, gradients, dithering, noise, a built-in pixel font, `scatter` brushes, tilemaps, random groups with reproducible seeds. - **Scenes**: layers, cast-shadow and light layers, per-layer PNG export. - **Animation**: frames as patches over a base sprite → strips + JSON tags + GIF. - **Lighting** (optional): lamps, glow, normal-based relief (see [`lighting.md`](lighting.md)). - **Errors** point at `file:line:col` and the asset/layer/op path, with "did you mean…" hints. Full API: [`reference.md`](reference.md). Agent workflow and essentials: [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md). ## Use it with an AI agent This repository is an agent skill: `SKILL.md` teaches the workflow (write → build → look at the preview → patch), `reference.md` holds the full API, and `lighting.md` is loaded only when needed. **Claude Code**: clone it into your skills folder, then ask Claude to draw something. ```sh # all projects git clone https://github.com/crsolver/claude-pxl.git ~/.claude/skills/pxl-pixel-art # or just one project git clone https://github.com/crsolver/claude-pxl.git .claude/skills/pxl-pixel-art ``` **Other agents** (Codex, Cursor, …): point them at `SKILL.md` and tell them the CLI is `node /bin/pxl.js`. Tip: ask the agent to start `pxl serve` so you can watch it paint in your browser. ## Development ```sh npm install # dev only: typescript, @types/node npm run check # type check + tests node scripts/gallery.ts # regenerate docs/gallery ``` ``` src/core/ engine, no Node APIs: image, palette + ramps, canvas ops, build, trace, project src/node/ vm sandbox loader, PNG/GIF encoders, outputs, CLI, live server src/viewer/ browser viewer (served type-stripped; no bundler) types/ pxl.d.ts globals for editor support in .px.ts files scripts/ build.js (dist/ for npm installs), gallery.ts examples/ example art files test/ node:test suites ``` In a clone the CLI runs the TypeScript sources directly. When installed as a package it runs `dist/`, which `npm install` / `npm pack` generate via `scripts/build.js` (Node won't strip types inside `node_modules`). ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

# 微信文本机器人框架
项目已在linux.do公开声明https://linux.do/


面向 Windows x64、微信 4.1.15.13 的 Python 插件框架。统一入口为 `main.py`，原生桥接负责文本收发，功能以插件加载。


# 本项目仅供学习，请勿用于违法行为

## 功能

- 文件传输助手、好友和群聊文本收发，以及真正的群艾特。
- 成语接龙：独立玩家、合并抢答和退出模式。
- `/绑定 昵称`：只设置当前群的称呼；不同群各自保存。未绑定时使用联系人缓存中的微信名。
- `/总结 昵称`、`/总结群聊`：通过配置的大模型总结当前群当天的文字记录。
- `/切换人格 嘴臭|卑微|夸夸|取消`：为当前群的对话、总结和接龙点评设置表达风格。
- 真正艾特机器人后对话，携带该成员在当前群当天此前最多十条有效发言。
- 每天北京时间 0 点清理旧日文本；`/清空` 手动清理当前群文本。
- 按文本长度随机等待后发送。
- 插件启停、重载与开发模板。

## 运行环境

Windows 10/11 x64、64 位 Python（已验证 Python 3.13）、`requirements.txt` 中的依赖，以及 Microsoft Visual C++ x64 运行库。

## 首次配置

在项目目录运行：

```powershell
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python tools/init_config.py
```

1. `bot_config.json`：将 `wechat_account` 改为自己的机器人微信 ID。绑定保存的是账号 ID，重新登录后 PID 改变不影响选择；多开时会等待指定账号，不改用其他账号。
2. `members_config.json`：在 `groups` 中添加自己要启用的群 ID，成员列表可以为空：

```json
{
  "database_file": ".runtime/member_data.sqlite3",
  "history_enabled": true,
  "daily_clear": true,
  "groups": {
    "12345678@chatroom": []
  }
}
```

3. `llm_config.json`：填写自己的 `api_key`、`base_url` 和 `model`。模板保留 DeepSeek 接口格式，密钥为空。
4. 模板默认关闭需要模型的 `idiom_chain`、`chat_summary`、`mention_chat` 插件。填写模型配置后，把它们的 `enabled` 改为 `true`。

账号 ID 必须是实际微信 ID；群 ID 以 `@chatroom` 结尾。`test` 消息会由 `id_responder` 插件回复当前会话 ID，`chats` 控制台命令可以列出本次连接收到消息的会话。所有示例 ID 和测试用名称均为虚构数据。

## 启动与验证

```powershell
python main.py --check
python main.py
```

`--check` 只检查配置、插件清单与语法，不注入微信，也不调用模型。正常运行前打开微信并登录配置中的账号。

也可以运行 `start_bot.ps1`：脚本优先使用项目的 `.venv`，其次使用 PATH 中的 Python；可通过 `-Python` 或环境变量 `WXBOT_PYTHON` 指定解释器，不依赖某台电脑的安装路径。

控制台命令：

```text
status
chats
members [群ID]
history 称呼 [条数]
plugins
enable 插件名
disable 插件名
reload [插件名]
quit
```

增加群、修改账号或成员配置后重启。停止时使用 `quit`，等待正常卸载原生桥接；微信可以保持打开。

`wechat_account` 设为 `null` 时，原生收发层可以选择唯一登录账号；启用成员目录和群记录需要明确配置机器人账号，以隔离不同账号的数据。

## 目录

```text
main.py                  统一入口
wxbot_framework/         框架、成员目录、消息缓存、大模型客户端
plugins/                 各功能插件和开发模板
native/                  原生桥接源码、两个必要 DLL、版本指纹和 MinHook
tests/                  本地测试
tools/                   本地配置初始化和发布前检查
```

# AutoFirma Web

Client-side-rendered SPA: sign and verify documents with X.509 certificates, entirely in the
browser. No backend, no key material leaving the client.

The reference implementation is [AutoFirma](https://github.com/ctt-gob-es/clienteafirma)
(`ctt-gob-es/clienteafirma`, the Spanish government's signing client, GPL-2+/EUPL-1.1): this
project re-thinks its signing core (`afirma-core`, the `AOSigner` family) as a browser-native
TypeScript app. See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for the map of the Java signing
core this rewrite follows, and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the repo rules.

The app lives at the repo root; from the root:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

## Stack

- SvelteKit 3 (static adapter) + Svelte 5 runes + Vite + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`)
- shadcn-svelte components (bits-ui) on the same tokens; dark mode is the `.dark` class on `<html>`,
  driven by the system preference from an inline script in `src/app.html` (#27)
- pnpm, Node 22 for builds
- Vitest + `@testing-library/svelte` + jsdom for the smoke test

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/routes/` | Pages — `/` is the sign flow |
| `src/lib/App.svelte` | Sign workflow shell (2/3 drop + file list, 1/3 sticky actions on ≥1024px; stacked below) and verify workflow |
| `src/lib/components/` | `FileDrop`, `FileCard`, `CertPicker`, `BatchQueue`, `VerifyReport` |
| `src/lib/components/ui/` | shadcn-svelte primitives (button, card, table, badge, input, dropdown-menu, dialog, tooltip) + their snapshot test (#27) |
| `src/lib/utils.ts` | `cn()` class merger used by the primitives |
| `components.json` | shadcn-svelte CLI config (`#lib` aliases, neutral base, `src/app.css`) |
| `src/lib/asn1.ts` | DER reader and writer (PKCS#12 / X.509 / CMS) |
| `src/lib/pkcs12.ts` | PKCS#12 container: PBES2 decryption, certificate bags |
| `src/lib/x509.ts` | Certificate summary (subject, issuer, validity, public key) |
| `src/lib/keystore.ts` | PIN + container → non-extractable `CryptoKey` + certificate list |
| `src/lib/cms.ts` | CAdES-BES detached `SignedData` (WebCrypto digest + hand-built DER) |
| `src/lib/sign.ts` | Format list and sign-flow types (the seam for #6–#11) |
| `src/lib/c14n.ts` | Canonical XML: C14N 1.0 + Exclusive C14N |
| `src/lib/xades.ts` | XAdES-EPES enveloped signature over an XML document |
| `src/lib/pades.ts` | PAdES B-B signing: CMS `SignedData` over a real PDF incremental update |
| `src/lib/pades-visible.ts` | Visible signature block: corner/page placement, image embedding, block text |
| `src/lib/der.ts` | Minimal DER writer/reader for the PAdES CMS structures |
| `src/lib/batch.ts` | Batch queue state machine, manifest and ZIP assembly (engine-agnostic) |
| `src/lib/zip.ts` | ZIP writer (STORE entries, CRC-32) — no dependency, verified by `unzip -t` |
| `src/lib/verify/` | Verification engine: DER/X.509/CMS, canonicalization, XMLDSig/XAdES, PDF/PAdES (`pades.ts`) |
| `scripts/fetch-roots.sh` | Refreshes the bundled FNMT trust anchor from fnmt.es (checks subject + fingerprint) |
| `scripts/smoke-real.sh` | Signs with a real keystore (`work/certs/*.p12`, gitignored) and verifies the result (#40) |
| `test/fixtures/` | Valid/tampered CAdES + XAdES samples, their generator and cross-check script |
| `src/lib/ooxml.ts` | OOXML (docx/xlsx/pptx) signing: XAdES v1.3.2 signature part, zip surgery via `fflate` |
| `src/lib/i18n.ts` | ES/EN copy |
| `Caddyfile` | Static hosting with SPA fallback (used by the root `Containerfile`) |
| `src/service-worker.ts` | App-shell precache, offline fallback and update handoff (PWA, #47) |
| `static/manifest.webmanifest`, `static/icon-*.{svg,png}` | Install manifest and icon set (#47) |
| `src/lib/components/PwaControls.svelte` | Header `Install app` / `Update version` buttons (#47) |

`#lib/*` subpath imports (`package.json` `imports`) map to `src/lib/*`.

## Commands

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # vite dev server
pnpm build        # static output in build/
pnpm preview      # serve build/ locally
pnpm test         # vitest smoke test (mounts App)
pnpm check        # svelte-check + tsc
pnpm verify:zip   # cross-check a batch ZIP with unzip -t and sha256sum
bash scripts/smoke-real.sh   # real expired-cert smoke test (skips without work/certs/*.p12)
```

## Verify flow (issue #8)

`Verificar` mode drops a `/.csig` (CAdES), `/.xsig` (XAdES) or PDF and reports one card per check,
green/red with the technical reason:

| Check | What it proves |
|---|---|
| Structure | the artifact parses as CMS `SignedData` / `ds:Signature`; a PDF's `/ByteRange` + `/Contents` delimit a PAdES signature |
| Content integrity | `messageDigest` signed attribute vs the digest of the embedded content (1) |
| Cryptographic signature | the signature over the DER re-encoded `signedAttrs` / over `c14n(ds:SignedInfo)` |
| Signed references | every `ds:Reference` transform chain (`enveloped-signature`, inclusive/exclusive C14N) reproduces its `DigestValue` |
| Signer certificate | the signer cert of the `SignerInfo`/`KeyInfo` |
| Certificate validity | the signer cert's validity window. Outside it the check is **amber, never red**: an expired signer makes the report `valid-but-expired` — the signature is still valid (#40) |
| Trust chain | issuer links verify by signature up to a bundled root (FNMT AC RAIZ FNMT-RCM) |
| Signing time | `signingTime` attribute / `xades:SigningTime` |

(1) detached CAdES cannot be checked alone: drop the original document when the report asks for it.
A detached PAdES needs no second file — the PDF's own `/ByteRange` spans are the content.

The overall verdict is `valid` (every check passed), `valid-but-expired` (only the signer's validity
window is over — a warning) or `invalid` (a check failed). `valid-but-expired` is what AutoFirma does
with an expired certificate, and it is what `scripts/smoke-real.sh` asserts against the real legacy
FNMT keystore in `work/certs/old-cert.p12`.

All crypto runs in the browser through `crypto.subtle` — certificates are parsed from DER by hand
(no new dependency), the trust store is the PEM under `src/lib/verify/roots/`, and unsupported
algorithms or transforms are reported as a red check with a reason instead of a silent pass.
Revocation (OCSP/CRL), *validating* a timestamp of an incoming signature and certificate policies
are out of scope. Timestamps can be **added** when signing, though — see the TSA section below.

Fixtures: `bash test/fixtures/generate.sh` rebuilds them (throwaway test PKI, keys gitignored),
`bash test/fixtures/verify-fixtures.sh` cross-checks them with `openssl cms -verify` and an
independent python digest recomputation. `pnpm test` runs that cross-check as part of the suite.

## Container

Build context is the repo root:

```bash
docker build -f Containerfile -t autofirme-web .
docker run --rm -p 8080:80 autofirme-web   # http://localhost:8080/
```

Multi-stage: `node:22-alpine` builds the static site, `caddy:2-alpine` serves it with the SPA
fallback (`try_files {path} {path}/ /404.html`).

## Installable app (PWA) — #47

`pnpm build` emits `build/manifest.webmanifest` and `build/service-worker.js`, and the prerendered
HTML registers the worker — all of it SvelteKit's own service-worker support (no plugin, no
dependency). The worker precaches the shell (`$app/manifest`'s built + static + prerendered files),
answers an offline navigation with the cached shell — signing still works with no network, because
nothing but the documents themselves ever leaves the browser — and never writes a runtime response
to a cache (`GET` + same-origin only, no `cache.put`), so a produced signature cannot be cached.

Chrome/Edge show **Install app** in the header when the browser fires `beforeinstallprompt`; the
button replays that prompt. A new deploy leaves a worker *waiting*, which shows **Update version**;
the click posts `SKIP_WAITING` and the page reloads once the new worker takes control.

Self-hosting notes:

- **HTTPS is required** for the service worker (and therefore for install) — the only exception is
  `http://localhost`. Behind a Cloudflare Tunnel the site is already HTTPS, so there is nothing to
  configure; on bare nginx/k3s, terminate TLS first.
- `.webmanifest` needs `application/manifest+json`. Caddy's Go mime table has no entry for it, so
  the `Caddyfile` sets it explicitly; on nginx add
  `types { application/manifest+json webmanifest; }`.
- Precached paths go through `$app/paths`, so a deployment under a subpath precaches `/subpath/…`.
- `vite dev` does not build the worker; check PWA behaviour with `pnpm build && pnpm preview`.
- The icons are generated from `static/icon.svg` / `static/icon-maskable.svg` (the seal from
  `App.svelte`, full-bleed teal `#008d80`, mark inside the maskable safe circle). Regenerate with:

  ```bash
  rsvg-convert -w 192 -h 192 static/icon.svg -o static/icon-192.png
  rsvg-convert -w 512 -h 512 static/icon.svg -o static/icon-512.png
  rsvg-convert -w 512 -h 512 static/icon-maskable.svg -o static/icon-maskable-512.png
  ```

## PKCS#12 support (no dependencies)

The container is parsed in the browser — no library, no server:

- **PBES2** (PBKDF2 + AES-CBC, what OpenSSL 3+/4 and Java 9+ write) and **legacy PBES1**
  (SHA-1 KDF + 3DES/RC2 — `src/lib/legacy-pbe.ts`, what the FNMT and Windows exporters write).
  A scheme outside those two is rejected with an actionable message instead of a half-parsed key.
- **BER, not just DER**: the envelopes the Windows/CryptoAPI exporter writes carry indefinite
  lengths and split every long string into chunks (`24 80 … 00 00`), including the implicit `[0]`
  of `encryptedContent`. The reader accepts both encodings.
- The private key is imported with `extractable: false` and `usages: ['sign']`, so its material
  cannot be read back out of the browser.
- The certificate that owns the key is identified by comparing public-key material (RSA modulus
  and exponent; EC public point) against each certificate of the container.
- The PKCS#12 MAC (RFC 7292 B.3) is verified when `MacData` is present: a mismatch is reported as a
  wrong PIN, and an unsupported MAC digest leaves the MAC unchecked rather than assumed.

## End-to-end smoke with a real keystore — #39

`scripts/smoke-real.sh` drives the whole loop — read the container, pick the signer, sign a document
with CAdES-BES, verify the produced `.csig` — through the app's own modules, for a **real keystore**
and for a **generated** one:

```bash
pnpm install                                   # the loop runs through src/lib, resolved by vitest
bash scripts/smoke-real.sh                     # real keystore + generated fixture
bash scripts/smoke-real.sh --no-generated      # only the real one
bash scripts/smoke-real.sh --cert work/certs/current-cert.p12 --pin-file .p12pass
```

- The real keystore and its PIN stay in gitignored files (`work/certs/*.p12`, `.p12pass`), are read
  at runtime and are never printed. A missing keystore or PIN file is skipped with a notice and
  **exit 0**, so the script is safe for anyone without a real certificate.
- Per keystore it asserts: `structure`, `contentDigest`, `signature`, `signerCert`, `certValidity`
  and `signingTime` are `pass`; the reported subject, issuer, serial and validity window equal the
  loaded certificate's; and the validity dates appear in the report output.
- Two oracles that are not this repository's code: `openssl cms -verify` over the produced `.csig`
  and the document, and `openssl x509 -subject -dates` over the signer certificate.
- The generated keystore is the self-signed RSA container of `src/test/fixtures.ts` (temporary,
  never committed). Its leaf is self-signed and its CA is not a bundled root, so `certChain: fail`
  is expected there — the signature checks are what it demonstrates.
- The report's `certChain` line is printed as it comes. Signing embeds only the signer certificate
  (#6), so even with the real FNMT keystore — whose container carries `AC FNMT Usuarios` — it reads
  `issuer certificate not included`, and verifying *your own* fresh `.csig` in the app shows a red
  *Trust chain* card. Embedding the chain is a separate change.
- `--cert work/certs/old-cert.p12` is expected to fail `certValidity`: that keystore expired
  2026-03-29 (issue #40 owns the expired-certificate path).

### The same loop in the UI (manual evidence)

The app opens in Spanish; the English labels are in brackets. Either keystore runs through it — the
real one (`work/certs/current-cert.p12`, PIN from `.p12pass`) or the generated fixture (PIN `1234`,
which this throwaway command materializes and prints the path of):

```bash
node --input-type=module -e "const { createPkcs12Fixtures } = await import('./src/test/fixtures.ts'); console.log(createPkcs12Fixtures().dir + '/modern.p12')"
```

1. `pnpm dev` and open `/`; the app starts in **Firmar** [Sign]. Open it from `localhost` or over
   https: away from a secure context the browser withholds WebCrypto entirely, and the app says
   so (banner + error) instead of pretending the file is broken.
2. In *2. Configura la firma* [2. Set up the signature], press **Agregar firma** [Add signature]
   and choose the `.p12`; type its PIN in **PIN de la firma** [PIN of the signature] and press
   **Guardar** [Save]: the container is sealed into this browser (IndexedDB), selected, and the
   modal closes on it. The file-shaped card fills in with the file name and the signer's `CN`:
   the certificate owning the private key is the one selected, and it is the only one that can
   sign (an expired one is flagged in red and still signs). Switching between **Firmar** and
   **Verificar** keeps that selection — the card just goes back to reading *Seleccionar firma*.
3. The card (**Seleccionar firma** [Select signature]) reopens *Firmas guardadas* [Saved
   signatures]: every sign ever added is a cell there, and the PIN is never stored — only the
   sealed container. **Agregar firma** inside the modal adds further `.p12` files the same way;
   a new one joins the grid instead of replacing the previous. Clicking a saved sign selects it
   and closes the modal; the first click of the visit asks that sign's PIN (the key cannot be
   used before it is unsealed), later clicks do not.
4. Drop the document in *1. Elige los documentos* [1. Choose the documents] and press **Firmar**
   [Sign]; the row turns to **Firmada** [Signed] and its **Descargar** [Download] saves the `.csig`
   (the same file is listed in the **Descargas** [Downloads] dialog, *Firmas generadas* [Produced
   signatures], with the signer and the file's SHA-256).
5. Switch to **Verificar** [Verify] and drop the `.csig`; a detached CAdES then asks for the
   original file under *Documento original* [Original document]. The report shows one card per check
   — *Estructura de la firma*, *Integridad del contenido*, *Firma criptográfica*, *Certificado del
   firmante*, *Vigencia del certificado*, *Cadena de confianza*, *Fecha de firma* — plus the signer
   identity (subject, issuer, serial) and its validity window.

## CAdES-BES signatures — #6

`src/lib/cms.ts` builds a **detached CAdES-BES** (`SignedData`, RFC 5652) whose four signed
attributes match the reference implementation: `contentType`, `messageDigest`, `signingTime` and
`signingCertificateV2` (ESS, RFC 5035). SHA-256 only; RSA (`rsaEncryption`) and EC
(`ecdsa-with-SHA256`, with WebCrypto's raw `r || s` re-encoded as a DER `SEQUENCE`) keys. The
document is **never** embedded — the `.csig` carries its digest, so the original file must be
kept next to it. The signature covers the whole `SET OF` signed attributes, and the digest and
signature come from `crypto.subtle`.

Cross-check (the oracle is OpenSSL, not our own code):

```bash
openssl cms -verify -inform DER -in contrato.pdf.csig -content contrato.pdf \
  -CAfile ca.pem -purpose any -binary
```

`-binary` matters: without it `openssl cms` applies S/MIME line-ending canonicalisation and
every signature of a file containing a newline would be reported as a content failure.
`src/lib/cms.test.ts` runs that command (plus `-cades` to force the ESS check) over freshly
generated RSA and EC containers, and compares the attribute set with the committed vector in
`src/test/fixtures/cades/` — a `.csig` generated once by `openssl cms -sign -cades -md sha256
-binary` (its signing key is not committed).

## XAdES support (no dependencies) — #7

XML documents are signed with an **enveloped XAdES-EPES** signature, entirely in the browser
(`src/lib/c14n.ts` + `src/lib/xades.ts`), and shipped as a `<name>.xsig` entry of the batch ZIP
(#9):

- **Canonicalization** is implemented here from the W3C specs: **C14N 1.0**
  (`REC-xml-c14n-20010315`) and **Exclusive C14N** (`xml-exc-c14n#`), which is what all the
  XMLDSig transforms and the `SignedInfo` canonicalization use.
- Two references: the whole document (`URI=""`, `enveloped-signature` + exc-c14n) and
  `xades:SignedProperties`. Digest and signature hash: SHA-256; `ds:SignatureValue` is a WebCrypto
  signature over the canonicalized `SignedInfo`.
- `ds:KeyInfo/X509Data` embeds the whole certificate chain loaded from the PKCS#12, and
  `xades:SigningCertificate` carries each certificate digest plus its issuer/serial.
- **Signature policy**: EPES wants a `SignaturePolicyIdentifier`; without one supplied by the
  caller the signature declares `<SignaturePolicyImplied/>` (nothing is invented — a real Spanish
  policy URN would have to come from the caller).
- The output is verified by **`xmlsec1`**, an independent XMLDSig implementation, in
  `src/lib/xades.test.ts` (its digests are recomputed by xmlsec1, so it doubles as the
  interoperability check for the canonicalizer). Tests also need `openssl` (fixtures, #5).

```bash
xmlsec1 --verify --enabled-key-data x509 --trusted-pem leaf.pem facturae.xml.xsig  # → status: OK
```

Not in scope: inclusive-c14n `InclusiveNamespaces` PrefixList on the transforms (supported by the
canonicalizer, unused by the profile), the Detached/Enveloping variants, timestamps and long-term
validation (XAdES-T/XL).

## Batch signing queue — #9

N documents can be dropped at once; they become a queue (`src/lib/batch.ts`) signed **one at a
time** with the chosen certificate, so the UI thread stays free between files and nothing is
uploaded. Each document carries its own status (`pending` / `signing` / `signed` / `error`):

- **Resumable**: a document that fails is recorded as `error` with the engine's message and the
  run continues; the next run only retries what is not signed yet.
- **Cancellable**: while a run is in flight the primary action becomes *Cancel*, which stops the
  batch at the next document (`phase: 'cancelled'`); the one already in flight finishes and keeps
  its signature — WebCrypto cannot be aborted mid-call — and the next run resumes from there.
- Replacing the document list mid-run abandons that run instead of writing results against the
  new list.
- A run ends in one ZIP (`src/lib/zip.ts`, STORE entries, hand-written CRC-32) with every signed
  document plus `manifest.json`: `signbatch` (`format`, `suboperation`, `algorithm`) and one
  `singlesigns` entry per document with `id`, `datareference`, `format`, `suboperation`, `result`
  (`BatchDataResult.Result` names: `NOT_STARTED` / `DONE_AND_SAVED` / `ERROR_PRE`), `description`
  on failure, plus `sha256`, `timestamp` and `output` as the issue asks.

Cross-checks: `src/lib/batch.test.ts` verifies each queued `.csig` with `openssl cms -verify` and
reads the archive back with an independent CRC-32 (`node:zlib`); `pnpm verify:zip` extracts a
generated archive with Info-ZIP and re-hashes its documents.

## PAdES B-B (`src/lib/pades.ts`) — #11

`signPdf(pdfBytes, options)` returns the signed document as the original bytes **plus an appended
incremental update** — the input is never rewritten or flattened:

- a `/Sig` field widget is added to the page `/Annots` and to the `/AcroForm` `/Fields`;
- its `/V` dictionary carries `/SubFilter /ETSI.CAdES.detached`, a `/ByteRange` covering everything
  except the `/Contents` hex string, and `/Contents` holding a CMS `SignedData` (detached, signed
  attributes content-type + signing-time + message-digest + signing-certificate-v2);
- RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 (`sha256WithRSAEncryption`) and ECDSA P-256/P-384 (`ecdsa-with-SHA256/384`) keys
  from `crypto.subtle`.

A **visible** signature (#45, `src/lib/pades-visible.ts`) adds an appearance stream inside the same
incremental update — so the drawn bytes are covered by `/ByteRange`, and the block can never
invalidate the signature:

- placed by page and corner (24 pt margin, 200×70 pt by default) or by explicit coordinates;
- the block carries an uploaded **PNG or JPEG** signature image (alpha honoured through `/SMask`),
  plus text lines: the signer's CN and the signing date, wrapped rather than cut.
- the sign panel exposes it as an off-by-default toggle with image upload, page number and corner
  picker; anything that is not a PNG/JPEG is rejected before the run starts.

Scope: PAdES baseline **B-B**, or **B-T** with `options.timeStamp` (RFC 3161, see below). Encrypted
inputs are rejected. The private key stays a WebCrypto `CryptoKey` in the browser.

Verification (`src/lib/pades.test.ts`) extracts the CMS and the byte-range content back out of the
produced PDF and verifies them with **openssl**, i.e. not with the signing code:

```bash
pnpm test        # golden fixture + RSA/ECDSA/visible signature, verified by `openssl cms -verify`
```

The signed output is also accepted by third-party tools (run against the committed fixture and
against freshly signed RSA, ECDSA P-256/P-384 and visible variants):

```bash
pdfsig -nocert test/fixtures/pades-b-b-signed.pdf   # "Total document signed" + "Signature is Valid."
qpdf --check test/fixtures/pades-b-b-signed.pdf     # exit 0, "No syntax or stream encoding errors"
pdftoppm -r 108 -png test/fixtures/pades-b-b-signed.pdf page   # page content still renders
```

`test/fixtures/` holds a one-page source PDF, a self-signed **test-only** RSA and EC key pair, and
the committed signed golden PDF. Regenerate the golden file after an intentional format change with
`PADES_WRITE_FIXTURE=1 pnpm test` (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 plus a fixed signing time make the output
byte-reproducible).

## Real-certificate smoke test (`scripts/smoke-real.sh`) — #35

End-to-end proof with a **real** certificate, outside the test suite (`pnpm test` only ever uses
the throwaway fixture PKI in `test/fixtures/`):

```bash
bash scripts/smoke-real.sh [input.pdf]     # signs + verifies; exits 0 on success
```

It reads the PIN at runtime from `.p12pass` (repo root, `chmod 600`, **gitignored — never commit
it**), loads `work/certs/old-cert.p12` through the shipped PKCS#12 reader and PAdES signer, writes
the signed PDF to `work/smoke-real-signed.pdf` (both `work/` paths are gitignored) and then
verifies the signature twice:

- the app's own verifier (`src/lib/verify`) over the CMS read back out of the produced PDF;
- `openssl cms -verify` on the same CMS and byte-range content, as an independent oracle.

The real container is PBES1 (`pbeWithSHA1And3-KeyTripleDES-CBC`, SHA-1 MAC), which WebCrypto cannot
decrypt; the script re-wraps it as PBES2/AES-256 with `openssl pkcs12` **into a temp dir**
(`mktemp -d`, removed on exit, temp PEM encrypted with the same PIN) and signs with that. Needs
OpenSSL 3+ locally. Missing `.p12pass` or container ⇒ skip notice, exit 0, so CI stays green.

An expired signer certificate is reported (`certValidity`) but not fatal: the smoke test asserts the
cryptographic checks (`structure`, `contentDigest`, `signature`) plus the openssl cross-check.

## Trusted timestamps (RFC 3161) — #43

`src/lib/timestamp.ts` builds a `TimeStampReq`, POSTs it to the TSA
(`Content-Type: application/timestamp-query`) and checks the reply before anything is embedded: the
`PKIStatus` must be granted, and the token's `messageImprint` must be the SHA-256 of the bytes we
asked about. Pass `{ timeStamp: '<tsa url>' }` to `signCadesDetached` (`src/lib/cms.ts`) or to
`signPdf` (`src/lib/pades.ts`) — or type the address in the sign panel, which is empty (no
timestamp) by default — and the token is added as the `id-aa-timeStampToken` **unsigned** attribute:
CAdES-T, or PAdES B-T for a PDF. The signed attributes are untouched, so the signature value is the
same one a B-B/BES signature would carry.

The imprint is the signature value, never the document (ETSI EN 319 122-1 §5.4): the TSA learns a
SHA-256 digest and nothing else — no document, no key, no certificate.

**CORS / self-hosting.** Most public TSAs (the ACCV one AutoFirma ships with included) send no CORS
headers, so a browser cannot POST to them directly. Nothing else is required for the core feature;
for a deployment that wants a specific TSA, put a same-origin path in front of it and type that path
in the panel. With Caddy, in the `Caddyfile` next to the app's `file_server`:

```
handle_path /tsa/* {
	reverse_proxy http://tss.accv.es:8318
}
```

nginx equivalent:

```
location /tsa/ {
	proxy_pass http://tss.accv.es:8318/;
	proxy_set_header Content-Type application/timestamp-query;
}
```

Tests never reach a TSA: `fetch` is stubbed and a throwaway `openssl ts` instance (fixture
certificate + config) answers with a real `TimeStampResp`, whose token and embedding are then
verified with `openssl ts -verify`.

## Status

Feature-by-feature comparison against the original desktop AutoFirma 1.9 — what is implemented,
what is deliberately impossible in a browser and what is still a gap — is in
[docs/PARITY.md](docs/PARITY.md).

Document selection, PKCS#12 certificate loading (#5), CAdES-BES signing (#6) and XAdES-EPES XML
signing (#7) work, and both formats run through the batch queue (#9): drop N files, sign them
sequentially and download one ZIP with the signed documents and `manifest.json`. The `.csig`
embeds only the signer certificate, not its chain.

PAdES B-B (#11) runs in the app too, verified against `openssl`, `pdfsig` and `qpdf`: pick PAdES-B-B,
optionally switch on the visible block (#45: signature image, page and corner), and the signed PDF
lands in the same batch queue and ZIP as the XML formats. Signatures can carry a trusted RFC 3161
timestamp (CAdES-T, PAdES B-T) when a TSA address is given (#43).

OOXML signing (#10) exists as a library (`src/lib/ooxml.ts`): it adds
`_xmlsignatures/sig-<uuid>.xml` (XAdES v1.3.2 EPES with MDSSI `SignatureTime`), the
`origin.sigs` origin part and its relationships, and leaves every other part byte-identical.
The UI does not call it yet — that wiring needs the certificate flow from #5.
