# Timestral

Blog post · Hugging Face collection · License

Timestral is a family of time series foundation models for multivariate probabilistic forecasting, with support for past-only and known-future covariates. This repository provides standalone inference for Timestral models. It needs only PyTorch, NumPy, `safetensors` and `huggingface_hub`, and runs on CPU or GPU. > **License:** the code in this repository is licensed under [Apache 2.0](LICENSE). The Timestral model weights are released separately on the Hugging Face Hub under a [Modified MIT license](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Timestral-209M/blob/main/LICENSE). See [License](#license). ## Highlights At launch, Timestral-209M ranked first among pretrained and zero-shot models on the three main public forecasting benchmarks: - 🥇 **GIFT-Eval**: #1 among pretrained and zero-shot models. - 🥇 **TIME**: #1 across 98 tasks. - 🥇 **fev-bench**: #1 across 100 tasks. All four sizes (5M, 28M, 123M, 209M) sit on the Pareto front of accuracy versus model size. Full results are in the [blog post](https://mistral.ai/news/timestral) and the model cards on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/collections/mistralai/timestral). - **Multivariate**: the variates of a series are forecast jointly. - **Covariates**: past-only, known-future and categorical. - **Probabilistic**: 21 quantiles per time step. - **Long context**: up to 32,768 steps. - **CPU-friendly**: no GPU needed for inference. ## Install ```bash pip install git+https://github.com/mistralai/timestral.git # Python >= 3.10, torch >= 2.4 ``` Or from a clone with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), using the versions pinned in `uv.lock`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/mistralai/timestral.git && cd timestral uv sync --frozen source .venv/bin/activate ``` ## Models The weights are on the Hugging Face Hub, in the Mistral AI organization: | model | Hub repo | weights (fp32) | |---|---|---| | Timestral-5M | [`mistralai/Timestral-5M`](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Timestral-5M) | 21 MB | | Timestral-28M | [`mistralai/Timestral-28M`](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Timestral-28M) | 111 MB | | Timestral-123M | [`mistralai/Timestral-123M`](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Timestral-123M) | 490 MB | | Timestral-209M | [`mistralai/Timestral-209M`](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Timestral-209M) | 837 MB | `from_pretrained` downloads `config.json` and `model.safetensors` once to the Hub cache. ## Forecast ```python import numpy as np from timestral import TimestralForecaster forecaster = TimestralForecaster.from_pretrained("mistralai/Timestral-209M") # device="cuda" for a GPU context = np.random.randn(2, 1, 2000).cumsum(-1) # (series, variates, time); NaN = missing forecast = forecaster.forecast(context, prediction_length=96) forecast.quantiles.shape # (2, 1, 96, 21): series, variates, horizon, quantile levels forecast.quantile_levels # (0.01, 0.05, 0.1, ..., 0.9, 0.95, 0.99) forecast.median # (2, 1, 96) forecast.quantile(0.9) # (2, 1, 96) ``` - `context` can be `(B, V, T)`, `(B, T)` (one variate per series) or `(T,)` (one series), as a NumPy array or a torch tensor. The variates of a series are forecast jointly. - NaN marks a missing value. `observation_mask` (same shape, False = missing) can mark more. - The context is capped at the trained length (32768 steps); the most recent steps are kept. - Horizons longer than one decode block (32 patches = 1024 steps) are forecast block by block; each block's median is fed back as context. ### Loading options `from_pretrained` takes a Hub repo id or a local directory with `config.json` and `model.safetensors`. - `revision` pins a branch, tag or commit; `cache_dir` and `token` work as in `huggingface_hub`. - `local_files_only=True` (or `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`) reads from the cache without network access. ### Covariates ```python forecast = forecaster.forecast( context, # (B, V, T) prediction_length=96, past_covariates=past, # (B, C_past, T): known over the context only known_covariates=known, # (B, C_known, T + 96): known over context and horizon ) ``` Covariates are conditioning rows: they are not forecast, and covariate rows never read the targets. Known-future covariate rows whose values are all 0 or 1 are treated as indicators. NaN marks a missing covariate value. ### Categorical covariates ```python forecast = forecaster.forecast( context, prediction_length=96, categorical_past_covariates=codes_past, # (B, C, T) numeric category codes, NaN = missing categorical_known_covariates=codes_known, # (B, C, T + 96) ) ``` Pass categories as numeric codes (for example `pandas.factorize`), with NaN for missing values and for any padding. For a univariate target each categorical row is target-encoded per series: category `c` becomes `(mean + sum_c) / (1 + count_c)` over the forward-filled context, missing values form their own category, and a category absent from the context maps to the series mean. Multivariate targets receive the raw codes. Encoded rows are appended after the numeric covariates. `timestral.covariate_encoding.target_encode` exposes the encoding. ## Architecture Timestral is a causal patch-based transformer trained with Decoupled Horizon Forecasting (DHF), where forecasts are generated from separate prediction tokens that read the causally encoded context. Each variate is a target, a past-only covariate or a known-future covariate: covariates pass information to targets but never read them, and only known-future covariates see the forecast horizon. A quantile head outputs 21 non-crossing quantiles per time step, and each forecast patch is denormalized with the statistics of the context and the block's earlier predicted medians. ## Benchmarks Timestral is evaluated zero-shot on three benchmarks, with the forecaster defaults and the full history up to 32768 steps as context: | benchmark | inputs beyond the target | |---|---| | [GIFT-Eval](https://github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/gift-eval) (97 configs) | `past_feat_dynamic_real` as past covariates | | [fev-bench](https://github.com/autogluon/fev) (100 tasks) | past and known covariates; categorical columns target-encoded | | [TIME](https://github.com/zqiao11/TIME) (98 tasks) | none (TIME has no covariates) | ## Contributing We do not accept pull requests. Bug reports and questions are welcome as [GitHub issues](https://github.com/mistralai/timestral/issues). timestral is maintained by the team at Mistral AI. We answer issues on a best-effort basis and fix security vulnerabilities and major bugs. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to report an issue. ## License The code in this repository (the `timestral` package and tests) is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file. The Timestral model weights are not covered by the Apache License 2.0. They are distributed separately on the Hugging Face Hub under a Modified MIT license, available in each model repository ([Timestral-5M](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Timestral-5M/blob/main/LICENSE), [Timestral-28M](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Timestral-28M/blob/main/LICENSE), [Timestral-123M](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Timestral-123M/blob/main/LICENSE), [Timestral-209M](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Timestral-209M/blob/main/LICENSE)). When using the model weights, you must not use them in a manner that infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates any third party's rights, including intellectual property rights.
